description: Deterministic, curated interaction pairs. Each rule carries a severity, a plain-language mechanism, a management action, and a named source. Severity is NEVER inferred from prose. This is a seeded, high-yield subset of what a licensed DDI database would provide (see docs/DATA_PROVENANCE.md); every rule here must be independently verified by a clinical pharmacist before production use.

sources.FDA_LABEL: US FDA approved product labelling (Section 7 Drug Interactions)
sources.STOCKLEY: Stockley's Drug Interactions (reference work; paraphrased, not reproduced)
sources.STOPP: STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people
sources.BEERS: AGS Beers Criteria for Potentially Inappropriate Medication Use in Older Adults

rules.title: Blood thinner + painkiller (NSAID) - bleeding risk
rules.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce platelet function and irritate the stomach lining, while warfarin reduces clotting. Together the risk of serious stomach or gut bleeding rises several-fold.
rules.management: Do not start an NSAID painkiller without speaking to the doctor who manages the blood thinner. If it is unavoidable, the doctor will usually add stomach protection and check the clotting test (INR) more often.
rules.citation: Warfarin sodium prescribing information, Drug Interactions - NSAIDs; BNF warfarin interactions

rules.title: Blood thinner + antiplatelet - additive bleeding risk
rules.mechanism: Two medicines that each reduce clotting are taken together, so bleeding is more likely and harder to stop.
rules.management: This combination is sometimes intentional after a stent. It must only continue under a cardiologist's instruction, with a plan for how long to take both.
rules.citation: Clopidogrel prescribing information, Drug Interactions

rules.title: Direct oral anticoagulant + NSAID - bleeding risk
rules.mechanism: The anticoagulant prevents clots and the NSAID impairs platelets and irritates the stomach, multiplying the bleeding risk.
rules.management: Prefer paracetamol for pain. If an NSAID is truly needed, it must be a short course decided by the prescriber, with stomach protection.
rules.citation: Apixaban / rivaroxaban prescribing information, Drug Interactions

rules.title: Blood pressure/heart medicine + potassium - high potassium risk
rules.mechanism: ACE inhibitors, ARBs and spironolactone all raise blood potassium. Adding a potassium supplement or taking two of these together can push potassium to a dangerous level, which disturbs heart rhythm.
rules.management: Do not take potassium supplements unless prescribed. Ask for a blood potassium test within 1-2 weeks of any change to these medicines.
rules.citation: Spironolactone prescribing information, Drug Interactions - ACE inhibitors and potassium supplements

rules.title: Two blood-pressure medicines from the same family - kidney and potassium risk
rules.mechanism: Combining an ACE inhibitor with an ARB (or either with spironolactone) increases the risk of kidney injury, low blood pressure and high potassium without adding much benefit.
rules.management: Usually only one of these is needed. Ask the prescriber to review the combination and check kidney function and potassium.
rules.citation: NICE guidance on dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin system

rules.title: Antidepressant + painkiller - stomach bleeding risk
rules.mechanism: SSRI/SNRI antidepressants reduce platelet function. Combined with an NSAID, the risk of stomach or gut bleeding increases roughly 3-4 fold.
rules.management: Use paracetamol for pain where possible. If both are needed, ask about a stomach-protecting medicine (a PPI).
rules.citation: Stockley's Drug Interactions - selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and NSAIDs

rules.title: Antidepressant + blood thinner - bleeding risk
rules.mechanism: The antidepressant reduces platelet function while the anticoagulant slows clotting; together the bleeding risk rises.
rules.management: Both are often needed. Do not stop either suddenly. Report unusual bruising, black stools or bleeding gums to the prescriber.
rules.citation: Stockley's Drug Interactions - SSRIs and anticoagulants

rules.title: Two serotonin-raising medicines - serotonin syndrome risk
rules.mechanism: Several medicines increase serotonin in the brain. Taking two together can cause agitation, sweating, shivering, muscle twitching, fast heartbeat and, in severe cases, high fever and confusion.
rules.management: Do not start or stop these together on your own. Seek urgent care for shivering, muscle twitching or high fever with confusion.
rules.citation: Linezolid / tramadol prescribing information, serotonin syndrome warning

rules.title: MAOI antidepressant mixed with another serotonin medicine - serious reaction
rules.mechanism: MAOIs combined with other serotonin-raising medicines can cause a severe, sometimes fatal reaction with very high fever and muscle breakdown.
rules.management: This combination is normally avoided. If both have been prescribed, contact the prescriber before the next dose.
rules.citation: Phenelzine / tranylcypromine prescribing information, contraindications

rules.title: Clopidogrel + omeprazole - reduced heart protection
rules.mechanism: Omeprazole blocks the liver enzyme that converts clopidogrel into its active form, so clopidogrel may work less well.
rules.management: Ask the prescriber whether pantoprazole or rabeprazole (which interfere less) would be a better stomach medicine for you.
rules.citation: Clopidogrel prescribing information, Drug Interactions - proton pump inhibitors

rules.title: Nitrate heart medicine + erectile dysfunction medicine - dangerous blood pressure drop
rules.mechanism: Nitrates and PDE5 inhibitors both widen blood vessels. Together they can cause a sudden, severe drop in blood pressure and fainting or a heart attack.
rules.management: The combination is avoided. Never take an erectile-dysfunction medicine within 24-48 hours of a nitrate - and tell any doctor treating chest pain that you take nitrates.
rules.citation: Sildenafil class labelling, contraindication with nitrates (nitrate list applies to all nitrates)

rules.title: Diabetes tablet + beta blocker - low sugar may be hidden
rules.mechanism: Beta blockers can mask the early warning signs of low blood sugar (shaking, fast heartbeat), so a hypo may be noticed only when it is more severe.
rules.management: Check blood sugar more often, especially after any dose change, and treat sweating or confusion as possible low sugar.
rules.citation: Beta blocker class labelling, drug interactions - hypoglycaemia masking

rules.title: Beta blocker + verapamil/diltiazem - slow heart rate risk
rules.mechanism: Both slow the electrical signals of the heart. Together they can cause a dangerously slow heart rate, low blood pressure, or heart block.
rules.management: This combination needs a cardiologist's supervision and a pulse check. Report dizziness, fainting or a pulse below 50.
rules.citation: Verapamil prescribing information, Drug Interactions - beta blockers

rules.title: Digoxin + amiodarone-type medicine - digoxin level rises
rules.mechanism: These medicines reduce how quickly digoxin leaves the body, so digoxin levels can rise into the toxic range, causing nausea, visual changes and dangerous heart rhythms.
rules.management: The prescriber will usually reduce the digoxin dose and check a digoxin blood level. Report nausea, loss of appetite, or seeing yellow-green halos.
rules.citation: Amiodarone prescribing information, Drug Interactions - digoxin

rules.title: Digoxin + water tablet - low potassium increases digoxin toxicity
rules.mechanism: Water tablets (diuretics) can lower potassium levels, which makes the heart more sensitive to digoxin and increases the risk of toxicity.
rules.management: Ask for potassium and kidney function checks, and report muscle cramps, palpitations or nausea.
rules.citation: Digoxin prescribing information, Drug Interactions - diuretics

rules.title: Two medicines that block dopamine - movement side effects
rules.mechanism: Both medicines block dopamine. Together they are more likely to cause stiffness, tremor, restlessness or involuntary movements, which are especially risky in older people.
rules.management: Ask the prescriber to review whether both are needed. Report any new stiffness, tremor or restlessness.
rules.citation: AGS Beers Criteria - antipsychotics and metoclopramide in older adults

rules.title: Several drying medicines together - confusion and falls risk
rules.mechanism: These medicines block acetylcholine. Adding them together causes dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, urinary retention and - importantly in older people - confusion and falls.
rules.management: Ask the prescriber how many of these can be reduced or replaced. Keep a list of all your medicines to make this review possible.
rules.citation: AGS Beers Criteria - anticholinergic burden in older adults

rules.title: Sleeping/calming medicine + strong painkiller - breathing depression
rules.mechanism: Both suppress the part of the brain that controls breathing. Together they can cause deep sedation, slowed breathing and, in older people, falls and confusion.
rules.management: This combination carries a serious warning. Use the lowest dose for the shortest time, never add alcohol, and treat excessive drowsiness as an emergency.
rules.citation: Opioid prescribing information - boxed warning for benzodiazepines

rules.title: Nerve-pain medicine + strong painkiller - sedation and breathing risk
rules.mechanism: Pregabalin/gabapentin add to the sedating and breathing-slowing effect of opioids.
rules.management: Ask the prescriber whether both are needed and at what dose. Report excessive drowsiness or slow breathing.
rules.citation: Gabapentin class labelling, Drug Interactions - opioids

rules.title: Statin + certain antibiotics/antifungals - muscle damage risk
rules.mechanism: These antibiotics and antifungals block the liver enzyme that clears statins, so statin levels rise and can cause severe muscle injury (rhabdomyolysis) and kidney damage.
rules.management: Statin doses are usually paused during the antibiotic course. Report muscle pain, weakness or dark urine immediately.
rules.citation: Simvastatin prescribing information - contraindications with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors

rules.title: Colchicine + certain antibiotics - colchicine toxicity
rules.mechanism: These medicines slow the removal of colchicine, which can then build up and cause severe - sometimes fatal - blood, muscle and organ toxicity.
rules.management: Doses are usually reduced or stopped during the interacting medicine. Report muscle weakness, numbness, unusual bleeding or fever urgently.
rules.citation: Colchicine prescribing information - boxed warning, fatal toxicity with CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors

rules.title: Allopurinol + azathioprine - dangerous blood count drop
rules.mechanism: Allopurinol blocks the enzyme that clears azathioprine. Azathioprine levels rise sharply and can suppress the bone marrow, causing severe anaemia and infections.
rules.management: This pair requires dose reduction (usually to a quarter) and close blood-count monitoring under a specialist. Do not change doses without the specialist.
rules.citation: Azathioprine prescribing information - boxed warning, allopurinol interaction

rules.title: Methotrexate + NSAID - methotrexate level rises
rules.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce how quickly methotrexate is cleared by the kidneys, so levels can rise and cause mouth ulcers, blood count falls and liver or lung injury.
rules.management: Occasional doses may be acceptable but must be discussed with the prescriber. Report mouth ulcers, fever, breathlessness or unusual bruising.
rules.citation: Methotrexate prescribing information - boxed warning, interactions

rules.title: Thyroid tablet + iron/calcium/antacid - thyroid tablet absorbed poorly
rules.mechanism: Iron, calcium and antacids bind levothyroxine in the gut so less of it is absorbed, and the thyroid dose can stop working properly.
rules.management: Leave at least 4 hours between the thyroid tablet and iron, calcium or antacid. Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach in the morning.
rules.citation: Levothyroxine prescribing information - Drug Interactions, absorption

rules.title: Certain antibiotics + antacid/iron/calcium - antibiotic stops working
rules.mechanism: Aluminium, magnesium, calcium and iron bind these antibiotics in the gut so very little is absorbed, and the infection may not clear.
rules.management: Take the antibiotic at least 2 hours before, or 6 hours after, the antacid, iron or calcium product.
rules.citation: Ciprofloxacin prescribing information, Drug Interactions - cation chelation

rules.title: TB medicine + blood thinner - blood thinner stops working
rules.mechanism: Rifampicin strongly speeds up liver enzymes that break down anticoagulants, so levels fall and the protection against clots can be lost.
rules.management: Anticoagulant doses usually need to be increased and monitored closely during and after the TB course. Never adjust without the prescriber.
rules.citation: Rifampicin prescribing information, Drug Interactions - anticoagulants

rules.title: Epilepsy medicine + blood thinner - blood thinner may stop working
rules.mechanism: Carbamazepine and phenytoin speed up the enzymes that clear many medicines, including anticoagulants, so blood thinner levels fall.
rules.management: Close anticoagulation monitoring is needed during any dose change of either medicine.
rules.citation: Carbamazepine prescribing information, Drug Interactions

rules.title: Steroid + painkiller - stomach ulcer and bleeding risk
rules.mechanism: Both steroids and NSAIDs damage the stomach lining. Together they multiply the risk of ulcers and serious bleeding.
rules.management: Avoid taking them together where possible, or use a stomach-protecting medicine as advised by the prescriber.
rules.citation: Stockley's Drug Interactions - corticosteroids and NSAIDs

rules.title: Blood pressure/water tablet + painkiller - kidney injury risk
rules.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce blood flow to the kidneys while ACE inhibitors/ARBs and diuretics also depend on kidney function - together (the 'triple whammy') they can cause acute kidney injury.
rules.management: Use paracetamol instead of NSAIDs where possible. If an NSAID is essential, ask for kidney function checks and keep the course short.
rules.citation: NICE CKD guidance - avoid NSAIDs in people on ACE inhibitors/ARBs and diuretics

rules.title: Lithium + painkiller/blood pressure medicine - lithium toxicity
rules.mechanism: NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs and diuretics reduce lithium clearance. Lithium levels rise and can cause tremor, vomiting, confusion and seizures.
rules.management: Lithium levels must be checked whenever these medicines are started or stopped. Report tremor, vomiting or confusion urgently.
rules.citation: Lithium prescribing information, Drug Interactions - reduced renal clearance

rules.title: Steroid + diabetes medicine - blood sugar rises
rules.mechanism: Steroids raise blood sugar. Diabetes medicines may no longer be enough while the steroid is being taken.
rules.management: Check blood sugar more often while on the steroid, and ask the prescriber whether the diabetes dose needs adjusting.
rules.citation: Corticosteroid class labelling - hyperglycaemia

rules.mechanism: Additive inhibition of platelet aggregation increases bleeding risk (dual antiplatelet therapy).
rules.management: This combination is often prescribed deliberately (for example after a stent). Do not stop either medicine on your own. Watch for unusual bruising, black stools, blood in urine or prolonged bleeding, and report them promptly.
rules.citation: Clopidogrel prescribing information: co-administration with aspirin increases bleeding risk; dual antiplatelet therapy is used under cardiology supervision.
rules.title: Two antiplatelet medicines together - bleeding risk
Aspirin + another painkiller (NSAID) - protection is reduced
rules.mechanism: Ibuprofen-type painkillers can block the antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin, so the aspirin may no longer protect the heart as intended, and the pair also increases stomach irritation and bleeding.
rules.management: If both are needed, take the aspirin at least 30 minutes before, or more than 8 hours after, the other painkiller - or ask the doctor about using paracetamol instead. Do not stop a prescribed low-dose aspirin on your own.
rules.citation: Ibuprofen prescribing information: concomitant use with aspirin may interfere with the antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin; FDA information for healthcare professionals on the concomitant use of ibuprofen and aspirin.

advisories.title: Metformin: pause during severe illness or before a contrast scan
advisories.mechanism: Metformin is cleared by the kidneys. If the kidneys are stressed - dehydration, severe infection, or an iodine contrast scan - metformin can build up and, rarely, cause a dangerous build-up of acid in the blood.
advisories.management: Pause metformin if you have severe vomiting, diarrhoea or dehydration, and tell the radiology team before any contrast scan. Ask when to restart. Avoid regular heavy drinking.
advisories.citation: Metformin prescribing information - boxed warning, lactic acidosis; contrast media

advisories.title: Thyroid tablet: take on an empty stomach, away from iron and calcium
advisories.mechanism: Levothyroxine is poorly absorbed when taken with food, iron, calcium or antacids.
advisories.management: Take it first thing in the morning with water, at least 30-60 minutes before food, and at least 4 hours away from iron, calcium or antacid products.

advisories.title: Long-term stomach acid tablets: ask about vitamin B12, magnesium and bone health
advisories.mechanism: Acid-suppressing tablets taken for months or years can reduce vitamin B12 and magnesium absorption and are associated with a slightly higher risk of fracture.
advisories.management: Ask the prescriber at least yearly whether the acid tablet is still needed, and whether B12, magnesium and calcium/vitamin D should be checked.
advisories.citation: Proton pump inhibitor class labelling - hypomagnesaemia, B12 deficiency, fractures

paracetamol.citation: Acetaminophen: maximum daily dose 4 g; lower limits advised in older/frail adults and chronic alcohol use

ibuprofen.citation: Ibuprofen prescribing information - maximally effective single dose 400-800 mg; lowest effective dose in older adults

aspirin.citation: Aspirin dosing - analgesic doses vs antiplatelet doses in older adults

changelog.change: each rule now declares mechanism groups; an alert fires only when the patient's ingredients span two different groups (prevents e.g. two NSAIDs triggering the SSRI+NSAID rule)
rules whose cited advice names a specific interval declare min_gap_hours, which the solver and the verifier enforce
every interaction rule now declares min_gap_hours explicitly (0.0 where timing cannot resolve the combination; 48.0 for nitrate/PDE5 washout). The solver no longer fabricates a severity-based gap.
